method: 1000/s one-factor comparisons assert identical realized product cohorts from item-keyed feed manifests; 3000/s crowded cases report effective admission and do not claim causal pairing if eligibility differs.

assumptions.exposure: Hardware exposure is unknown. Nominal 100 us and stress 500 us are ASSUMED. Blur pixels = 3 m/s * exposure seconds * 4000 px/m; image formation uses a centered fractional box integration over pixel cells, so timestamps represent exposure midpoints.
assumptions.latency: Exposure changes image formation only. It is distinct from the existing 4 ms pipeline latency floor; every scenario keeps a 60 ms minimum total controller latency.
assumptions.noise_nominal: ASSUMED well-lit sensor: Gaussian shot-noise approximation at 16 photoelectrons/DN plus 1 DN RMS read noise.
assumptions.noise_stress: ASSUMED lower-light sensor: Gaussian shot-noise approximation at 4 photoelectrons/DN plus 3 DN RMS read noise.
assumptions.jitter: ASSUMED sinusoidal 8 Hz physical belt-speed variation of +/-5%; controller layout remains at nominal 3 m/s.
assumptions.touching: ASSUMED crowded feed uses a +/-60 mm lane and 0.2 mm minimum spawn surface gap; physics may bring beans into contact but spawning forbids penetration.
assumptions.runtime: Synthetic sensor-transform wall cost is reported separately and excluded from measured detector/controller CPU. Runs make no real-time claim.

limits: One physical run per scenario; intervals are binomial sampling intervals, not between-run uncertainty.
Synthetic transform runtime is not camera hardware time and is excluded from detector/controller CPU.
Effective admitted rate is reported because crowded spawning may not sustain the requested feed.
Final outcomes cannot by themselves identify whether vision, tracking, timing, contacts, or jets caused an error.
